$reconciliation.$note: Settled 2026-08-30 by https://github.com/mohamedsamy911/dga-kit/blob/master/harvest/reconcile-tokens.py against DGA stylesheet build PDaQ7SHU. The kit previously described the gap between what DGA declares and what this file carries as 'aliases and per-component role vars resolving to values already carried'. That was WRONG and is retracted: 516 declarations resolve to values this file does not hold. See https://github.com/mohamedsamy911/dga-kit/blob/master/harvest/RECONCILIATION.md for every one.
$reconciliation.$genericPaletteNote: DGA's stylesheet ships the whole upstream Untitled-UI ramp - blue, cyan, fuchsia, indigo, moss, orange, pink, purple, red, teal, violet, yellow and seven separate grey ramps. Those are not Platforms Code colours and are deliberately not carried. The defect was never STATING that exclusion, not making it.
$reconciliation.$dgaNamespacedNote: A real coverage gap: 240 DGA-namespaced declarations resolve to values this file does not hold - the whole --alpha-* transparency scale (49), --tag-* (29), --notification-* (22), --button-* (17), --featuredicons-* (17), --link-* (16), --border-* (15), --form-* (14) and more. Triage listed in https://github.com/mohamedsamy911/dga-kit/blob/master/harvest/RECONCILIATION.md.
$reconciliation.$historicalNote: The figure 1,052 quoted before this reconciliation came from a 2026-08-26 browser getComputedStyle read of :root. The stylesheet parse gives 1,065 declared on :root and 1,126 distinct names overall. Different methods measuring different things; both are recorded rather than one silently replacing the other.

The dark theme is NOT among them: DGA publishes it in the public CSS and this file carries it under role.dark - but for AUDIT ONLY, because upstream it is unactivatable. See role.dark.$activation.

$verify.issue: DGA ships 402 dark declarations in its public CSS, under the selector `[data-theme=dark] :root` - which can never match, because :root is <html> and a descendant combinator needs an ancestor it does not have. dark.$comment: Dark-theme semantic roles. DGA ships 402 dark declarations; these are the 62 that remap the text and background roles captured above, plus 5 backgrounds dark does NOT remap (carried at their light values, which is what they compute to). The other 340 - link, button, tag, form, featuredicons, border, icon, notification, controls, stepper, table, tooltip - are uncaptured HERE and in the light theme too, by the same scope decision. All 402 are in https://github.com/mohamedsamy911/dga-kit/blob/master/harvest/raw/2026-08-27-dark-theme-roles.json.
dark.$activation: NONE. These values are held for AUDIT ONLY and are deliberately not generated into tokens.css. DGA ships them under [data-theme=dark] :root, which can never match, so upstream the theme is inert - and inert is safe. Correcting the selector would activate 1.05:1 pairings for any consumer already using data-theme="dark" (Chakra v3 does, out of the box). See $verify.

$verify.issue: DGA's own selector can never match. :root is <html>, and a descendant combinator requires :root to HAVE an ancestor carrying [data-theme=dark]. <html> has none. Verified in the live page: querySelectorAll returns 0 with the attribute on <html> and on <body>, and no computed value changes. The bundle contains no prefers-color-scheme rule, no .dark class, and zero instances of the correct :root[data-theme=...] form - so there is no alternative activation path. DGA ships a complete dark theme that cannot turn on.
$verify.action: Retain the values for audit; do NOT emit a corrected selector into any shipped stylesheet. Report the defect to DS-DGA@dga.gov.sa - the fix is theirs to make, and if they make it the theme goes live everywhere at once. Guarded by 'generated CSS ships no live dark rule' in https://github.com/mohamedsamy911/dga-kit/blob/master/evals/validate-fixtures.py. Evidence: https://github.com/mohamedsamy911/dga-kit/blob/master/harvest/raw/2026-08-27-dark-theme-spike.md.

$verify.issue: The five *-light status surfaces are NOT remapped by the dark block, so they keep their near-white light values while text.default flips to #ffffff. White on #f3fcf6 is 1.05:1 - the worst pairing in either theme, and effectively invisible. This is more severe than the text.error problem below.
$verify.action: Do not use these surfaces in dark mode. DGA publishes no dark tint for them anywhere - every variant it ships (notification-, tag-, featuredicons-) still resolves to the same near-white value - so this is the reason a dark stylesheet cannot be made safe from DGA's own values, and the reason this kit generates none. An entity that needs dark mode substitutes its own tint and records it in dga-brand-overlay. Caught by check-contrast.mjs --theme dark.

$verify.issue: Dark keeps red.700 for error text. On the dark surfaces it measures 2.68:1 (body), 2.87:1 (white) and 2.21:1 (card) - fails AA at every size on every dark surface. An error message nobody can read.
$verify.action: Substitute red.300 (#fca19b) - DGA's own choice for notification.text-error and controls.control-text-error in dark, so it is cited, not invented. Record the substitution in dga-brand-overlay. Audit-only here; nothing is generated.

$verify.issue: The brand green is not remapped for dark. 3.71:1 on background.body - large text only, down from a marginal 4.75:1 pass in light. The primary brand text colour stops being usable for body copy.
$verify.action: Large text only in dark, or substitute primary-sa-flag.300 (#88d8ad), which text.primary-light already uses and which measures 10.46:1.

$verify.issue: Recorded so the light-theme finding is not over-generalised: the gold that fails at 2.30:1 on every LIGHT surface PASSES at 7.64:1 on background.body in dark. The role is not inherently broken - it is in the wrong theme.
$verify.action: Cite the 2.30:1 failure as a light-theme finding, not an absolute one.

$verify.issue: Two hazards. (1) DGA publishes this as -2%, and CSS letter-spacing does not accept percentages - they were proposed in css-text-4 and never shipped, so a browser silently drops the declaration. tokens.json keeps -2% because it is what DGA publishes; generate-tokens.mjs converts it to -0.02em on the way out. (2) Arabic is a connected script - letter-spacing breaks the joins.
$verify.action: Never emit -2% into CSS. The generator converts percentages to em; if you hand-write tracking anywhere, write -0.02em. Scope it to Latin or zero it under [dir="rtl"] - tokens.css ships a guard rule. Do NOT "fix" this value in tokens.json: it is the harvested value and a re-harvest must diff clean.
